title: Machine learning-based risk prediction model for postoperative acute kidney injury in surgical patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD): development, validation, and SHAP-based explainability

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Machine learning-based risk prediction model for postoperative acute kidney injury in surgical patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD): development, validation, and SHAP-based explainability》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p6】The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database provides a rich and granular dataset encompassing pre-, intra-, and postoperative variables for ICU patients. Using this database, we aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model for predicting postoperative AKI in surgical patients with CKD. While the present model focuses on tabular clinical data, it serves as a foundational step toward next-generation dynamic, multimodal, and clinically integrated perioperative kidney protection systems. Our approach integrates logistic regression, ensemble learning, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) functions to assess nonlinear associations with the ultimate goal of providing clinically interpretable and actionable predictions to support perioperative decision-making and improve renal outcomes.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) is no longer regarded as a random postoperative complication; rather, it represents a predictable perioperative emergency that unfolds within a fragile physiological environment characterized by reduced nephron reserves, impaired autoregulation, and heightened vulnerability to hemodynamic and inflammatory stressors [1–4]. In CKD patients, even subtle perioperative perturbations may trigger rapid deterioration in renal function, suggesting that AKI follows discernible and potentially modifiable trajectories rather than unpredictably [5,6]. Consequently, modern perioperative nephrology increasingly demands forward-looking, real-time intelligence systems capable of anticipating evolving renal stress and initiating preemptive protective strategies before irreversible injury occurs [7,8]. Against this backdrop, machine learning-based prediction represents a critical first step toward transforming AKI prevention from reactive risk estimation to proactive, anticipatory renal protection.

【Introduction · S0001-p2】Patients with CKD are particularly vulnerable to postoperative AKI because of reduced nephron reserves, impaired autoregulation, and increased susceptibility to hemodynamic fluctuations and nephrotoxic exposure [9–11]. Evidence suggests that even minor renal insults can lead to persistent kidney dysfunction, potentially accelerating progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) [12,13]. The occurrence of postoperative AKI in CKD patients has been strongly associated with increased in-hospital mortality, prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay, and greater long-term dialysis dependence [14–16].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Machine learning-based risk prediction model for postoperative acute kidney injury in surgical patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD): development, validation, and SHAP-based explainability》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Prediction performance of machine learning models on the validation set · S0004-p1】The receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves of the nine machine learning models are presented in Figure 1, illustrating their ability to discriminate between patients with and without postoperative AKI. Among all the models, XGBoost achieved the highest AUC of 0.844, indicating excellent discriminatory performance. This was followed by Random Forest (AUC = 0.822) and LightGBM (AUC = 0.804), both of which showed strong prediction capabilities. Traditional logistic regression and SVM also demonstrated comparable performances, with AUCs of 0.793 and 0.791, respectively. KNN and MLP showed moderate performance (AUC = 0.795 and 0.782, respectively), whereas AdaBoost and Naive Bayes yielded lower AUC values of 0.656 and 0.636, respectively, suggesting limited discriminative power. Overall, the ROC analysis highlighted that ensemble-based models, particularly XGBoost and Random Forest, outperformed conventional classifiers in predicting postoperative AKI in patients with CKD.

【Prediction performance of machine learning models on the validation set · S0004-p2】The predictive performance of the nine machine learning models was evaluated using five key metrics: accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. The results are shown in Figure 2. Among all the models, XGBoost consistently outperformed the others, achieving the highest values across nearly all metrics, including AUC (0.844), accuracy (0.791), sensitivity (0.79), specificity (0.80), and F1-score (0.73). Random Forest and LightGBM also demonstrated strong predictive abilities, with AUCs of 0.822 and 0.804, respectively, and F1-scores of 0.68 and 0.70, respectively. The logistic regression model achieved moderate performance (accuracy, 0.733; AUC, 0.793; F1-score, 0.62), whereas MLP and SVM also showed balanced but slightly lower predictive values. In contrast, Naive Bayes and AdaBoost exhibit poor performance. Naive Bayes yielded the lowest AUC (0.636) and F1-score (0.57), whereas AdaBoost showed lower accuracy (0.754) and sensitivity (0.69) than the other models. Overall, tree-based ensemble models (XGBoost, Random Forest, and LightGBM) performed better than traditional classifiers in predicting postoperative AKI with higher discriminative power and classification balance.

【Data availability statement · S0009-p1】The data sets used and analyzed in this study are available from the first author and the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

【Statistical analysis · S0002-S2007-p1】Continuous variables are summarized as mean ± standard deviation (SD) for normally distributed data or median with interquartile range (IQR) for non-normal data. Categorical variables are presented as frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between the AKI and non-AKI groups were performed using the Student’s t-test or Mann–Whitney U test for continuous variables and the chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, as appropriate. Multicollinearity among the predictors was assessed using the variance inflation factor (VIF), with a threshold of VIF >5 indicating potential collinearity. All statistical analyses were conducted using R software (version 4.2.2) and Python (version 3.9) with the relevant packages, including glmnet, Boruta, randomForest, XGBoost, lightgbm, SHAP, pROC, caret, and rmda. A two-sided p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
